([[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]]) | college = * [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] (2021–2022) * [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] (2022–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 13 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2024 | years1 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | highlights = * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] (2024) * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2024) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman team (2022) }} '''Devin Carter''' (born March 18, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]] and the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. Carter was selected with the 13th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==Early life and high school career== Carter initially attended [[Cherry Creek High School]] in [[Greenwood Village, Colorado]]. He transferred to [[Doral Academy Preparatory School]] in [[Doral, Florida]], after his freshman year, when his family relocated to Florida following his father, [[Anthony Carter (basketball)|Anthony Carter]], being hired as a player development coach for the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=Basketball recruiting: South Carolina could land Devin Carter|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-recruiting/phil-kornblut/article242239816.html|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=April 23, 2020|access-date=February 14, 2024}} Carter's senior season was cut short due to a shoulder injury, and he opted to enroll at [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], for a [[postgraduate year]].{{cite web|first=Collyn|last=Taylor|title=After reclassifying to be a Gamecock, Carter showing potential as freshman|url=https://southcarolina.rivals.com/news/after-reclassifying-to-be-a-gamecock-carter-showing-potential-as-freshman|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=January 28, 2022|access-date=February 20, 2024}} Carter was rated a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] during his senior year at Doral Academy.{{cite web|first=Collyn|last=Taylor|title=Gamecocks land commitment from high-scoring guard|url=https://southcarolina.rivals.com/news/gamecocks-land-commitment-from-high-scoring-guard|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 24, 2020|access-date=February 14, 2024}} ==College career== ===South Carolina=== On December 13, 2021, Carter was named [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Freshman of the Week. He helped [[2021–22 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] to a 66–65 win over [[2021–22 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. He led the team with 16 points, which tied his career high, and 7 rebounds.{{cite web |title=Carter Named SEC Freshman of the Week |url=https://gamecocksonline.com/news/2021/12/13/mens-basketball-carter-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week/ |website=University of South Carolina Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |date=13 December 2021}} On March 8, 2022, Carter was named to the SEC All-Freshman team. He became the 13th Gamecock to be named to the SEC All-Freshman squad. He joined [[Michael Carrera]], [[Sindarius Thornwell]], [[A. J. Lawson]] and [[Jermaine Couisnard]].{{cite web |title=Carter Named to SEC All-Freshman Team |url=https://gamecocksonline.com/news/2022/03/08/mens-basketball-carter-named-to-sec-all-freshman-team/ |website=University of South Carolina Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |date=8 March 2022}} Carter played in 30 games during the 2021–22 season and started in seven of them. He averaged 9 points and 3.8 rebounds during the season.{{cite web |title=Devin Carter |url=https://gamecocksonline.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/devin-carter/ |website=University of South Carolina Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |date=5 August 2021}} ===Providence=== As a sophomore, Carter transferred to [[Providence College|Providence]].{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Koch|title=Two transfers — South Carolina's Devin Carter and La Salle's Clifton Moore Jr. — commit to PC|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2022/04/17/south-carolina-shooting-guard-devin-carter-and-la-salle-big-man-clifton-moore-jr-both-committed-the/7350509001/|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=April 17, 2022|access-date=February 14, 2024}} He averaged 13 points and 4.9 rebounds in his first season with the Friars.{{cite web |last=Koch |first=Bill |date=March 31, 2023 |title=Providence basketball stars Bryce Hopkins, Devin Carter will remain Friars |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2023/03/31/providence-basketballs-bryce-hopkins-devin-carter-to-remain-friars/70068886007/ |access-date=February 14, 2024 |work=[[The Providence Journal]]}} In his second season at Providence, under first-year head coach [[Kim English (basketball)|Kim English]], Carter won both [[Big East]] First Team and [[Big East Player of the Year]].{{cite web|first=Fisher|last=Brewer|title=Former Gamecock star Devin Carter drafted in Lottery Round of the NBA Draft.|url=https://www.si.com/college/southcarolina/basketball/former-gamecock-star-devin-carter-drafted-in-lottery-round-of-the-nba-draft-01j1bj2g2mrr|work=Sports Illustrated|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 26, 2024}} He averaged nearly 20 points and 9 rebounds per game, establishing himself as one of the best players in college basketball. His outstanding scoring ability, tenacious defense and high motor impressed NBA scouts throughout his junior season. ==Professional career== On June 26, 2024, Carter was selected with the thirteenth overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Rivera|title=Sacramento Kings select Devin Carter with 13th pick of 2024 NBA draft. What to know|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2024/06/26/devin-carter-nba-draft-2024-sacramento-kings/74208894007/|work=USA Today|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 26, 2024}} and on July 9, he signed with the Kings.{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Sign Devin Carter|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-devin-carter|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=July 10, 2024}} Throughout his rookie season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Stockton Kings Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Stockton-Kings/56/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 2, 2025}} On January 3, 2025, Carter made his NBA debut against the [[2024–25 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]] and his father Anthony, an assistant coach for the Grizzlies. He recorded no points, 5 rebounds and 2 assists.{{cite web|first=Kailee|last=Bryant|title=Kings rookie Devin Carter makes NBA debut against Grizzlies under father's watch|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/kings-rookie-devin-carter-makes-nba-debut-against-grizzlies-under-fathers-watch/ar-AA1wVJy1|website=MSN.com|date=January 3, 2025|access-date=January 4, 2025}} On October 14, 2025, the Kings exercised the third-year option on Carter.{{cite web|title=Kings Exercise Team Option on Devin Carter|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-exercise-team-option-on-devin-carter|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2025|access-date=October 16, 2025}} On March 10, 2026, Carter recorded a career-high 24 points in a 114–109 victory over the [[2025–26 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web|title=Kings' Devin Carter: Tallies career-high 24 points|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-devin-carter-tallies-career-high-24-points/|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On April 10, Carter increased his career high to 29 points, also setting career highs in rebounds (nine) and three-pointers (six) during a 124–118 win over the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web|title=Devin Carter scores 29 points to lead the Kings to a 124-118 win over the Warriors|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/devin-carter-scores-29-points-044200684.html|access-date=2026-05-04|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en|date=2026-04-11|last=Dubow|first=Josh}} On June 30, 2026, Carter and a 2033 second-round pick were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Alpha Kaba]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Guard Devin Carter |url=https://hawks.com/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-guard-devin-carter |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=hawks.com |language=en|date=2026-06-30}} ==Personal life== Carter is the son of [[Anthony Carter (basketball)|Anthony Carter]] and Cassie Carter. He has one brother named Joshua.{{cite web|title=Devin Carter - Men's Basketball|url=https://friars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/devin-carter/9383|work=Providence College
